svg.aria-label: How each decision calls the models, with one real decision as the example. Belief: one call on the public history returns each card's odds of being in each hand, drawn as a heatmap; 66 deals are sampled from it, drawn as tiles, and 2 that break earlier play are crossed out, leaving 64 sampled deals. Prior: one call on 64 positions scores every card; the 64 legal plays are drawn as bars and the top 8 are admitted, J♦ at log-odds −0.06 and A♣ at −0.22 first. Value: 4 calls of 128 positions score each of the 8 plays in all 64 deals, drawn as an 8 by 64 heatmap with a row-mean column; the best average was the ace of clubs at 1.799. Endgame: with 7 cards or fewer, no model call; each deal is solved exactly by a game tree with all hands face up and pruned branches, and the per-deal results are averaged; it switched to the jack of diamonds, 1.797 against 1.719 for the ace of clubs. It played the jack of diamonds in 0.49 seconds. All models run in NumPy on the server CPU with a 3 second budget per decision; the trump call and the bury reuse the value model.
svg.title: One decision, four steps
svg.text: Example: one live lead with 7 cards left. Numbers are real; cell shades, tiles and tree shape are illustrative.
All models run in NumPy on the server CPU · budget 3 s per decision · trump call and bury reuse the value model
